quote: Sleep quality improved in the app group, t(28) = 2.20, p = .036.
Mood differed across the three arms, F(2, 57) = 3.41, p = .04.
Adherence depended on age band, chi2(3) = 6.80, p < .05.
Minutes of use correlated with wellbeing, r = .31, p = .038, n = 45.
Baseline wellbeing (single 1-7 item) averaged 5.19 in the 28 controls.
The 25 app users averaged 3.48 on the same item.
Across all 150 screened people the mean was 2.47.
21 of the 62 completers (35.0%) used the app daily.
We randomized 90 participants: 30 to app, 31 to diary, and 28 to waitlist.
Good sleep was more likely with the app (OR 1.89, 95% CI 1.21 to 2.95, p = .005).
The risk of dropout was higher on the waitlist (RR 2.40, 95% CI 1.10 to 3.20).
Insomnia remission was more frequent (OR 1.45, 95% CI 0.92 to 2.28, p = .03).
Wellbeing rose by 4.2 points (95% CI 1.1 to 7.3; p = .008).
Total sleep time increased, t = 2.5, p = .02.
